newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX oil prices end sharply lower on Feb expiry.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX oil prices end sharply lower on Feb expiry.

text.p: NYMEX oil prices declined sharply Friday reversing a two-day rally as traders unloaded positions from the expiring February refined product contracts and sold heating oil amid bearish weather forecasts.

"At first, we had forecasts for below normal temperatures but now they are saying it's going to be normal to above normal next week," said Michael Busby, trader with Northville Industries in Melville, New York.
February heating oil settled off 1.69 cents at 68.65 cents a gallon while February gasoline settled off 1.35 cents at 68.47 cents a gallon.
The February contract in refined products expired Friday requiring traders to liquidate positions in the nearby month.
"Crude tends to follow refined products on their expiry," said Busby. March crude settled off 72 cents at $24.15 a barrel.
Prompt crude fell to a session low of $24.10, where it held trendline support extending on a spot continuation chart from the low November 6 of $22.47 and through the low on December 11 of $23.15.
In the last two sessions, spot heating oil rose 4.10 cents on short covering ahead of the Feb expiry.
But, dealers said traders were setting long positions in the March contract amid the bullish momentum. Bearish weather forecasts Friday then resulted in abrupt profit-taking, dealers said.
Independent forecaster Weather Services Corp saw temperatures moderating to normal to slightly above normal next week in the northeastern United States, the largest heating oil market in the world.
((-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761))
